messages:
support-james: Heads up — we got a customer escalation from ACME: sudden p99 jump on generate/stream route after last roll (around 11:15). They report conversational responses sometimes taking 4-6s (used to be ~1.2s). Sending graphs: https://redwood.internal/obs/graphs?panel=acme_p99

sre-oncall-ryan: looking. Opened a short triage. Any recent batching changes in the deploy? :mag:

maria-eng: deploy-bot shows the runtime image bump v1.19.2 -> v1.19.3 at 11:02. That patch included a change to continuous-batcher defaults (linger_enabled=true, hold_for_ms increased from 6 -> 25).

olivia-eng: confirmed in config diff: 
```
continuous_batcher:
  max_batch_size: 64
  min_batch_size: 1
  hold_for_ms: 25  # used to be 6
  max_wait_ms: 40
  greedy_coalesce: true
  enable_linger: true
```

kevin-sre: ACME traffic is mostly tiny prompts (avg tokens per request ~18) and pretty spiky. Increasing hold_for_ms would let more requests be coalesced into batches, which saves tokens but increases tail latency for sporadic requests.

support-james: customer says p95 also degraded for some endpoints; they're sensitive to p99. They asked for mitigation asap.

sre-oncall-ryan: quick mitigation options I can push: 1) disable linger/coalesce for that tenant, 2) decrease hold_for_ms back to 6, 3) route ACME to a low-latency pin (dedicated pool) if available. Which should we try first?

maria-eng: I'd flip hold_for_ms -> 6 for the fleet to roll back the regression quickly, but that affects cost. Prefer targeted fix: tenant routing or per-tenant batch overrides. Can we hotpatch per-tenant policy?

olivia-eng: we have per-tenant policy overrides feature. I can push a policy for tenant acme_corp to set `hold_for_ms=6` and `enable_linger=false` for now. PR #4921 ready, will apply via console if SRE approves.

kevin-sre: do it. Also raise alerting for batch_hold_percent where p99 > 2s. Add a dashboard panel for small-prompt cohort so we catch this earlier.

ops-bot: deploy-bot reported rollout start for policy override PR #4921 at 11:38.

support-james: applying now — I told the customer we're doing a targeted rollback.

sre-oncall-ryan: after override, I see p99 drop back to ~1.4s in the next minute on the ACME tenant traces. Looks like the override helped. Monitoring now. :white_check_mark:

maria-eng: good. We should still understand root cause: the combination of `enable_linger` + higher `hold_for_ms` selectively penalized tiny, bursty tenants. We should add a canary checklist for batcher config changes.

olivia-eng: agreed. Repro steps I used locally: 
1) spawn 40 clients sending 1-2 small prompts each with random inter-arrival (Poisson).
2) run with previous config and new config, collect p99.
Example command: 
```bash
python tools/repro_load.py --clients 40 --rate 200/s --prompt-file samples/small_prompts.txt --duration 120s --endpoint /generate
```
Observations: new config increases p99 by ~3-4x for this pattern.

kevin-sre: logging note: we should instrument batch composition metrics (batch_size histogram, hold_time distribution) with tenant tag. That would have pointed the finger faster. Filing ticket.

sre-oncall-ryan: created ticket SRE-708: "batcher telemetry per-tenant + hold_time histograms" and assigned to kevin-sre.

support-james: customer update: "Thanks for fast response, latency normalized after your change. Please follow up with root cause." They want timeline for permanent fix.

maria-eng: plan: (A) revert fleet default to previous conservative defaults in next patch; (B) land per-tenant throttle/override UI so we can do targeted tweaks; (C) add canary + traffic-pattern tests for batcher defaults. I'll own (A), Olivia owns (B), Kevin owns (C).

olivia-eng: adding a short-term mitigation: add a feature flag to disable greedy_coalesce per-tenant. Pushed PR to staging, test tomorrow AM.

kevin-sre: I'll add dashboards + alerts: - panel: batch_size_by_tenant (p50/p95/p99) - panel: hold_time_histograms - alert: tenant_p99_latency > SLA threshold for 5m

ops-bot: policy override PR #4921 deployed successfully at 11:44.

sre-oncall-ryan: closing the immediate escalation. Leaving the thread open for follow-ups and the tickets. Thanks team. :tada:

support-james: noted owners and timeline to customer. They asked for a short writeup — I'll draft and share.

maria-eng: draft for postmortem/learnings: keep conservative defaults for continuous-batcher, require load-profile test before changing coalescing parameters, add per-tenant telemetry, and ensure a fast rollback path. Will post doc later today.
